text:
Maya R: Quick question — for billing/invoice boundaries should we stamp tenant/billing tags at ingress (API/gateway) or derive them later during enrichment? We're seeing a few mismatches when org<>billing-account mappings change during rollouts.

Aj Patel: I'd vote for ingress stamping. Keeps dedupe keys and immediate metrics consistent with what the customer will be invoiced for.

Kevin L: Ingress stamp is simpler for downstream attribution, yes, but it means the ingress layer must be fully authoritative/trustworthy. That increases attack/poisoning surface if anyone can spoof tags. We should at minimum sign the tag or issue a short-lived proof.

Maya R: Signed tag sounds reasonable. Do you mean a signature header from auth service? e.g.
```json
{
  "event_id": "evt_...",
  "tenant_tag": "acct_ABC",
  "billing_account": "bill_XYZ",
  "tenant_sig": "hmac(...)"
}
```

Samir (billing): Billing system only cares about billing_account boundaries. Many customers have multiple orgs under a single billing account. We need two concepts: resource_owner (org) and billing_account (invoice boundary). Whatever we stamp at ingress must include both.

Aj Patel: Good point. Operationally that means the ingress should call auth/tenant-service to expand opaque tokens into {resource_owner_id, billing_account_id} and attach a signed envelope. Latency cost though.

Kevin L: Alternative: accept a provisional minimal tag at ingress (resource_owner) and do async enrichment to attach billing_account_id later, emitting a "finalize_billing_tag" event that updates accounting. Tradeoff: immediate dashboards might show provisional costs until finalize runs.

Maya R: That provisional approach reduces tail latency but complicates invoice correctness and audit trails. How do we handle charge corrections if finalize changes attribution?

Samir (billing): We must have an immutable provenance chain. If finalize changes attribution, emit a correction event that debits/credits the affected billing_account entries and surface those corrections in a monthly reconciliation window. Also surface corrections in invoice notes.

metering-bot: Reminder: raw_ingest and raw_events are kept for 30 days currently. Any proposed scheme that needs longer auditability will need retention change + storage cost estimate.

Kevin L: Proposal (schema): add top-level fields in metering event: "billing_boundary" (billing_account_id), "resource_owner", "tag_proof" (signed token), and "provenance_chain" (list of event ids). We keep the raw_ingest pointer so finalizers can point back.

Aj Patel: Operational plan idea:
- Ingress: attach provisional tags + nonce + sign with ingress-key
- Enrichment workers: async join to billing metadata, emit finalize or correction events
- Pipeline: accept provisional attribution for realtime metrics; mark records as "tentative"
- Billing: only charge based on finalized records; corrections applied as journal entries

Maya R: Sounds reasonable. Concern: how many corrections backfills do we accept before charging customers unexpectedly? Need a policy: e.g., 72h window for free automatic corrections, beyond that manual review.

Samir (billing): +1 to 72h auto window. Anything older becomes "historical adjustment" and goes through billing ops. Also add telemetry: correction-rate per customer and per-environment.

Kevin L: Also think about security: ingress should rotate signing keys and we should verify signatures in the enrichment/finalize step. We might use a short-lived JWT from auth service instead of static HMAC.

Aj Patel: Action items: 1) spec new event schema (billing_boundary, resource_owner, tag_proof, provenance_chain) 2) perf test ingress call to tenant-service and measure p50/p99 3) define correction/backfill policy (72h auto, >72h billing ops) 4) estimate retention change if we need >30d raw_ingest for audits 5) write migration/backfill playbook for existing untagged events

Maya R: I'll draft the RFC with those action items. @Kevin @Aj @Samir please add objections or missing items. :thumbsup:

Aj Patel: No objections from me. Will add perf numbers once I run a small experiment. :eyes:

Samir (billing): I'll add billing-side UX for corrections and how adjustments surface on invoices.

Kevin L: I'll sketch the key-rotation and signature verification flow. Also note we should special-case internal service accounts to avoid extra hops.

Maya R: Great, thanks everyone.
